newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills three, wounds 20 in Algiers - residents.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills three, wounds 20 in Algiers - residents.

text.p: At least three people were killed and about 20 wounded by a bomb on a minibus operating between the Algiers districts of El Harrach and Oued Smar on Thursday, residents said.
They told Reuters by telephone the bomb wrecked the bus, one of numerous private small buses that serve a network of routes in Algiers.
"There were at least three dead among the passengers, and around 20 wounded," one resident said.
There was no official comment on the blast, the second in two days in the area.
Several bombs have exploded on trains and buses and been blamed by officials on Moslem rebels trying to topple the government.
On Wednesday, residents in El Harrach said a bomb that morning wounded about 40 people aboard a train near the suburb.

On Thursday, El Watan said two bombs had exploded in the first two coaches of the train and 46 people were wounded. Le Matin newspaper also reported two bombs on the train and said two people had been killed and around 50 wounded.
Earlier this week, the authorities imposed new security on the capital, Algiers, home to around 3.5 million people, to thwart bombings.
They said it was now compulsory for officials to check people going to shops, buses, coach stations, government and private business buildings, cinemas and theatres. Cars also had to be checked.
The last major train attack killed 21 people and wounded 20 in the south Algiers suburb of Gue de Constantined in April.
El Watan also said 11 "terrorists", Algeria's official term for Moslem fundamentalists, had been killed by security forces in Saida province, southwest of Algiers on Tuesday.
